items.prompt: White to move. Choose a sensible sixth move. Several moves are within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best, so more than one answer is accepted.

claims.statement: At depth 16 Nf3, Rc1, cxd5 and Qc2 are all within 0.4 pawn of the best move.
The knight on g1 has not moved yet.

hints: What does White still have at home: a knight, a rook, the queen?
Think of a developing move that does not close the centre or release the tension for nothing.
The knight on g1 can go to f3, or a rook or the queen can step to the c-file.
items.explain: White's kingside knight is still at home, and the rooks and queen have not yet chosen a file. Nf3 develops the knight and prepares to castle; Rc1 and Qc2 prepare the c-file; cxd5 releases the tension on d5. At depth 16 all four moves are within 0.4 pawn of the best move, so the choice is about plans, not about a single correct move.

feedback_by_move.g5f6: [I] Trading the bishop now removes the piece that pressures d5 and lets Black free the position without a fight.
feedback_by_move.h2h3: A waiting move; it does not develop a piece.

items.prompt: Black to move, in the position of the last board after 10.Be2. Name a reasonable move. Two trades of the knight are possible.

claims.statement: At depth 16 Nxc3 and Nd7 are both within 0.4 pawn of the best move.

The knight on e4 faces the knight on c3.
Take on c3, or develop the other knight.
items.explain: Black's knight on e4 stands opposite White's knight on c3. Taking it continues the plan of simplifying. Developing the other knight keeps the tension. At depth 16 both moves are within 0.4 pawn of the best move.

items.prompt: Black to move, with the pawn on b6 and White's bishop on d3. Tap every square the bishop on c8 can move to.

claims.statement: The bishop on c8 can go to a6, b7 and d7.
The bishop on c8 attacks b7 and d7.

hints: The bishop moves along diagonals from c8. Which diagonals are open now?
One diagonal runs down to the left, one down to the right.
The left diagonal reaches b7 and a6. The right one reaches d7 only, because e6 holds a pawn.
items.explain: Before ...b6 the bishop had one move. With the pawn on b6, the diagonal c8-b7-a6 is open: b7 and a6 are free. The other diagonal, c8-d7-e6, still stops at d7 because Black's own pawn stands on e6. Three moves instead of one.

items.prompt: White to move. The pawn on d5 looks loose, and it is tempting to take it with the knight. Count before you take. Find a safe move (two are fine).

claims.statement: At depth 16 e3 and Nf3 are both within 0.4 pawn of the best move.
At depth 16 Nxd5 is worse than the best move by at least four pawns.
The pawn on d5 is attacked once, by the knight on c3.
The pawn on d5 is defended once, by the knight on f6; the knight on d7 blocks the queen.

hints: Which white piece attacks d5? What happens if it takes?
After Nxd5 Nxd5 the bishop on g5 attacks something, but Black has a check.
Develop a piece or support the centre instead; Nf3 and e3 are both fine.
items.explain: After 6.Nxd5 Nxd5 the bishop takes the queen, but the black bishop gives check from b4 and takes White's queen in return, so White loses a piece. A safe sixth move such as e3 or Nf3 keeps the position equal. At depth 16 e3 and Nf3 are within 0.4 pawn of the best move, while Nxd5 is worse by at least four pawns. After the knight leaves c3 the check on b4 can only be answered by Qd2, so the queen is traded back and White has lost a knight for a pawn. The pawn on d5 was not loose: it is attacked once (Nc3) and defended once (Nf6), because the knight on d7 blocks the queen's defence.

feedback_by_move.c3d5: The Elephant Trap: Nxd5 Nxd5, Bxd8 Bb4+, and White loses material.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find a sound move (several are fine).

At depth 16 ...e5 is worse than the best move by at least two pawns.

hints: Ask what each of White's pieces attacks before you choose a plan.

Moves that keep the structure and wait, or that strike at d4 or c4, are all sound.
items.explain: Five moves are within 0.4 pawn of the best at depth 16: the waiting moves a6 and a5, the break c5, the capture dxc4 and b6, which prepares the bishop. The pawn push ...e5 is not among them: it is worse by at least two pawns.

items.prompt: White to move. Which file is half-open for White here, so that a rook belongs on it?

claims.statement: The c-file is half-open for White and the e-file for Black.
Black's queenside majority is a7, b6, c7, d5.

hints: A half-open file for White has no white pawn on it, but a black pawn does.
White has no c-pawn. Which black pawn stands on the c-file?
The pawn on c7 stands alone on the c-file, so a white rook on c1 looks at it.
items.explain: White has no c-pawn, so the c-file is half-open for White: the rook on c1 looks at Black's pawn on c7. Black has no e-pawn, so the e-file is half-open for Black. The pawn on d5 is not on a half-open file because White's pawn on d4 stands on the same file. This is an exchange structure like Carlsbad, with Black's pawn still on c7.
